clue.text: Irish warder making drink available?

definitions.note: a phrase describing what the tool does, standing in for the noun; the question mark admits the looseness

parts.note: Cork is an Irish county and city, so the word stands for something Irish
screw is old prison slang for a warder or prison officer

explanation.surface: An Irish prison officer quietly lets the inmates get hold of alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: CORK is an Irish county and city; SCREW is British prison slang for a warder. The definition describes the tool by what it does: it opens bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: The tool pulls stoppers from wine bottles, which is how the wine becomes available to pour.

clue.text: Winning position for a sound European partner

indicators.note: the word for the European is taken as it is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a Czech is a European from the Czech Republic
a mate is a partner or companion

explanation.surface: A reliable continental friend is in a strong spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective (reliable) describing the European; it signals that CZECH is taken as heard, CHECK.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, putting the opposing king in an inescapable attack wins the game.

clue.text: It assists helicopters going up and down

indicators.note: in a down clue the word reads the same upwards as downwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A gadget helps aircraft rise and descend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up and down' sounds like flight; it says the entry reads the same both ways down the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotating blade assembly on top of a helicopter provides its lift.

clue.text: Accidentally erase end of composition

indicators.note: by accident the letters get jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wipes the closing bars of a piece by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A song or piece of music performed in the evening for a beloved is a musical piece.

clue.text: Make fun of one man endlessly breaking regulation

indicators.note: the other pieces break into the rule, splitting it

parts.note: a rule is a regulation
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Dick is a man's name

explanation.surface: A lone fellow keeps flouting the rules and mocking everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last letter of the name, and 'breaking' splits the regulation word after its first letter to take the inserted pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean mock or deride, holding someone up to scorn.

clue.text: Drink for a prisoner upset about everything

indicators.note: the turned letters go round the other piece
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so read bottom to top

parts.note: POW stands for prisoner of war
all means everything

explanation.surface: A captive, angry about everything, wants a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the prisoner abbreviation to WOP, and 'about' wraps that round the word for everything. The answer is British slang for beer.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for beer or other alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Bedding belonging to the Parisian surgeon

parts.note: French du means 'of the', so a Parisian's word for belonging
a vet is an animal surgeon

explanation.surface: A French doctor's own quilt is under discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: A continental quilt filled with down or fibre is a common item of bedding.

clue.text: After a month, agree to garage's finishing this overhaul

indicators.note: the word for agreeing comes after the month

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December
OK means agree, as a verb

indicators.note: the finishing letter of the word garage's

explanation.surface: A motorist leaves the car at the garage for a month for a service.
explanation.walkthrough: To decoke an engine is to clear carbon deposits from its cylinders, part of an overhaul.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing carbon from an engine's cylinders and valves was a routine part of servicing a car.

clue.text: He glosses over the crookedness of van hirers

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters of van hirers are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone covers up the dishonesty of people who rent vans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glosses over' suggests covering up; literally it means applying a glossy coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who applies a shiny protective coat to wood literally puts a gloss over it.

clue.text: Playhouse? Not at that place

indicators.note: the theatre does not have the letters of at

parts.note: a playhouse is a theatre
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor says the theatre is not where he is.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb points to a place away from the speaker, the opposite of here.

clue.text: Came on stage and made a record

explanation.surface: An actor walked on and then cut a disc.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor comes on through a door onto the stage, and putting something in a register or log is recording it.

clue.text: Source of chlorophyll in Switzerland

explanation.surface: A plant pigment is being traced to its Swiss origin.
explanation.definitionFit: The forage plant also called alfalfa is green and leafy, rich in pigment; the same name belongs to a Swiss city and lake.

clue.text: Girl in pink, a renowned model

indicators.note: the girl's name sits inside the run of words that follows, across their boundaries

explanation.surface: A famous fashion model is dressed in pink.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name, so it fits a clue asking for a girl.

clue.text: Strikes may result when hands are thus advanced

definitions.text: Strikes may result when hands are thus advanced

parts.words: Strikes may result when hands are thus advanced
parts.note: the strikes are not industrial action and the hands are not workers: moving a clock's hands round in their usual direction makes it chime the hours

explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikes' and 'hands' suggest a labour dispute; they are the chimes of a clock and its pointers.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock's hands move to the right round the dial, and pushing them on past the hour sets off the chimes.

clue.text: Drink publicised first in Yorkshire

indicators.note: the publicised word goes in front of the drink, so it comes first

parts.note: something publicised has been aired, broadcast or made known
ale is a drink, a type of beer

explanation.surface: A drink is advertised first of all in a northern county.
explanation.walkthrough: The district is a valley in Yorkshire, northern England, which also gives its name to a terrier breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The valley of the River Aire is a district of Yorkshire, so it is a place found in that county.

clue.text: Proving wrong about nanny's aggressive action

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a nanny is a female goat, and a goat attacks by butting

explanation.surface: Disproving claims that a children's nurse turned violent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nanny' suggests a children's nurse; it is a nanny goat, which butts with its head.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut an argument is to refute it, showing it to be false.

clue.text: Stylish city without a function

indicators.note: the city loses the letters that follow, as if going without them

parts.note: Chicago is a major American city
a function is a go, from the verb: a machine that works is said to go

explanation.surface: A fashionable town has no event worth attending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' suggests a party; here it is the verb meaning work or run, as in 'the car won't go'.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart and elegant in dress or style, a fashion word borrowed from French.

clue.text: Read about a son of Priam securing backing for a horse

indicators.note: the word for reading goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to con is to study or read carefully
Paris was a son of Priam, king of Troy

explanation.surface: Someone studies a Trojan prince while placing a bet on a racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing for a horse' suggests a bet; it is a cloth laid over a horse's back. 'securing' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental cloth laid over a horse's back and saddle is a decorative covering for it.

clue.text: Student intervening in scold's punishment gets the bird

indicators.note: the student's letter comes between parts of the punishment

parts.note: nagging women were once punished on the ducking stool, plunged into a pond
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A pupil who steps in to stop a nagger being punished is jeered.
explanation.walkthrough: A scold was a nagging woman; in old England she could be punished on a ducking stool, plunged into water. 'gets the bird' suggests being booed.
explanation.definitionFit: A young duck is a bird.

clue.text: Like Doctor. Aquinas. introducing a plant?

definitions.note: the question mark admits the definition hides behind a clue that reads as theology

parts.note: Thomas Aquinas was called the Angelic Doctor, so like him is angelic

explanation.surface: A saintly scholar brings in a new herb.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Aquinas was known as Doctor Angelicus, the Angelic Doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall aromatic herb whose candied stems decorate cakes is a garden plant.

clue.text: Bale out of this mountainous island

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of Bale are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to parachute out of a plane over a hilly isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bale out' reads as abandoning an aircraft; 'out' is the anagram signal on Bale.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean island off Tuscany where Napoleon was exiled is rugged and hilly.

clue.text: Smuggler on horseback? Not in the first place

parts.note: a runner smuggles goods, as in a gun-runner or rum-runner
a jockey who is up is riding, mounted on the horse

explanation.surface: A mounted contraband carrier is told he did not win.
explanation.definitionFit: The one who finishes second in a race or contest did not take the top position.

clue.text: Good husbandry caused most of the disagreement.

indicators.note: the word the loses its last letter, leaving most of it

parts.note: a rift is a disagreement or split

explanation.surface: Careful farming was at the root of the quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husbandry' suggests farming; it means careful management of money and resources.
explanation.definitionFit: Husbandry in its old sense is careful, economical management of resources.

clue.text: Directs attention to particulars.

explanation.surface: Someone singles out the details.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate with a finger is to direct notice; a list of separate items or details is a list of particulars.

clue.text: Gun found, in church in a Derbyshire town

indicators.note: the abbreviation for church is found inside the name of the town

parts.note: Matlock is a town in Derbyshire, in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: A firearm has turned up in a church in a Derbyshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: MATLOCK is a spa town in Derbyshire, in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: An old musket fired by a slow match lowered into the pan was a kind of firearm.

clue.text: Creature observed low. over. Kent

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
Kent is a county in South East England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: An animal was seen lowing across the fields of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is the verb for a cow's call, not the opposite of high. Kent is a county in South East England.
explanation.definitionFit: The large North American deer is an animal.

clue.text: An old senator's source of wine

explanation.surface: A Roman politician supplies the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Senators were literally the senior men of Rome's council; the hedgerow tree's berries and flowers are made into country wine.

clue.text: Build barrier without engineers? A vain hope

indicators.note: without means outside here, so the barrier goes round the engineers

parts.note: to dam a river is to build a barrier across it
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Hoping to put up a wall with no engineers is foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' seems to mean lacking; here it means outside. The Royal Engineers are a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: An unrealistic aspiration or fantasy is called a pipe dream, a fond wish.

clue.text: Macbeth bought golden ones from all sorts of people

definitions.text: Macbeth bought golden ones from all sorts of people

parts.words: Macbeth bought golden ones from all sorts of people
parts.note: Macbeth tells his wife he has won high regard from everyone, in Shakespeare's line about buying golden views of himself from all sorts of people; 'ones' stands for the missing noun

explanation.walkthrough: The clue quotes Macbeth, Act 1 Scene 7: 'I have bought golden opinions from all sorts of people'. 'Ones' stands in for the missing word, given in the singular.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth's line refers to the high views others hold of him, their judgements or beliefs about him.

clue.text: Frigidity is around since fracas

indicators.note: the word is wraps round the scrambled letters
a fracas is a noisy disturbance, so the letters of since are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A coldness has hung about ever since a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fracas' rearranges the second word to CINES, and 'around' puts the first word round it. 'Frigidity' could suggest a manner; it is literal coldness.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean coldness, literally of ice or figuratively of manner.

clue.text: A number took courses in speaking

indicators.note: spoken out, the word for having eaten matches a different spelling

parts.note: to eat the courses of a meal is to have eaten them: ate

explanation.surface: Someone working through a set menu is counted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took courses' looks like studying; it means ate the courses of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a cardinal figure, the one after seven.

clue.text: Distinguished bishop, possibly, controlling 22

definitions.note: a participle phrase describing the railway worker; 22 is the answer to 22 down, the movable rails at a junction

parts.note: signal as an adjective means notable or distinguished, as in a signal honour
a bishop is one example of a chess man, hence the 'possibly'

explanation.surface: An eminent churchman is put in charge of some particulars.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 down (POINTS) is used in its railway sense: the movable rails a signal box worker sets at a junction.
explanation.definitionFit: The railway worker in a signal box operates the levers that switch the track at junctions.
